status_note: The client calls a POI-5-only adaptation API (IOUtils.setByteArrayMaxOverride) in production, so the adaptation is causally POI-5-triggered. NOT yet differential-verified (the break has not been reproduced in this repo's own code).
discovery_method: Phase 2 external mining: GitHub code search for the POI-5 adaptation signature 'setByteArrayMaxOverride', then find_adaptation.py-style history check.

behavioral_break.why_it_breaks: POI 5.0 introduced a default maximum byte-array size in IOUtils; reading data larger than the default throws at runtime, so extraction/parsing silently fails (returns null / errors). Compiles fine against POI 5 -> behavioural, not syntactic. The fix is to raise the limit via IOUtils.setByteArrayMaxOverride(n) -- an API that exists ONLY in POI 5, so calling it is causally POI-5-triggered.

adaptation.author: Brett Meyer
adaptation.summary: Raised POI's byte-array limit to Integer.MAX_VALUE (effectively disabling it) to cope with POI 5's new default cap.
adaptation.caveat: The call was committed inside a large multi-purpose WIP commit, so it is bundled with unrelated changes -- not a clean same-commit dependency-bump + fix like the xstream/chainsaw case.

verification.differential_needed: Build the repo, apply the POI 4->5 bump to pre-adaptation code, and confirm the byte-limit break manifests in this repo's own usage, then that setByteArrayMaxOverride resolves it (or a generated mimic test).
verification.standalone_repro_note: A standalone mimic (IOUtils.toByteArray with a large declared length) was attempted 2026-07-01 and did NOT reproduce the break: POI's byte cap is enforced deep in its document/record parsing, not at the top-level API (toByteArray just allocates until OOM). A faithful repro needs a crafted document or the repo's own parsing path (repo build required). Unlike xstream's one-call ForbiddenClassException, this parser-internal break is not standalone-reproducible.
verification.conclusion: Signature-confirmed POI-5 production adaptation; full BBC verification pending (standalone mimic insufficient - see standalone_repro_note).
